answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a scarce, slashable bond: each identity locks tokens, and randomly selected peers audit its signed actions against independent evidence. If an agent submits fabricated work or double-claims a task, a successful challenge burns its bond and redistributes part to the challenger. Spawning a dawn comet of mirror identities then yields no extra voting weight without extra locked capital, while each fraud attempt risks that capital; the defense costs the attacker funds and time, not merely a new email address.
